newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica unions slam hike, seek central bank reform.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica unions slam hike, seek central bank reform.

text.p: The Congress of South African Trade Union (Cosatu), the country's largest labour movement, said on Thursday that a recent bank rate rise would hit workers and threaten small businesses with closure.
Cosatu warned that thousands of employees were now at risk of losing their jobs and called for reform of the central Reserve Bank.

The Reserve Bank announced a rise in its key Bank rate to 17 percent from 16 percent on Wednesday in a move the bank said necessary given an unstable rand, rising short-term money market rates and the threat of higher inflation.
"Cosatu and other organisations who believe in the developmental monetary policy condemn the policy of Dr Chris Stals to keep the interest rate extremely high," Cosatu said.
"Once more Dr Stals and the Reserve Bank are being allowed to use monetary policy to squeeze consumers, workers and small businesses who depend on borrowing in order to survive."
Cosatu said that a parliamentary commission should be established to look at current monetary policy and consider reforms of the Reserve Bank, including putting union representatives on its board.
